main_grievance: Consumer wants Equifax to delete late-payment marks they say are inaccurate on a credit account.

elements.condition: Respondent is a consumer reporting agency
Consumer disputed the completeness or accuracy of an item in their file
Agency failed to reasonably reinvestigate or correct

evidence_quote: if the completeness or accuracy of any item of information contained in a consumer's file at a consumer reporting agency is disputed by the consumer and the consumer notifies the agency directly, or indirectly through a reseller, of such dispute, the agency shall, free of charge, conduct a reasonable reinvestigation to determine whether the disputed information is inaccurate
rationale: A dispute of late-payment data sent to a credit reporting agency triggers the agency's reinvestigation duty in 1681i(a)(1); the template's TILA citations do not change the respondent.

main_grievance: Card issuer treats payments the consumer says were made (ACH, then debit card) as late and demands a much larger payment.

elements.condition: Creditor on a consumer credit card account
Consumer made a payment
Payment received by the creditor but not credited as of the date of receipt
Delay in crediting results in a finance or other charge

evidence_quote: A creditor shall credit a payment to the consumer's account as of the date of receipt, except when a delay in crediting does not result in a finance or other charge or except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section.
rationale: The core dispute is whether the issuer credited the payment on receipt, which is the duty in 1026.10(a). 1026.13 (failure to credit a payment is a billing error under 1026.13(a)(4)) requires a written notice, and the consumer only called.

main_grievance: Bank denied the consumer's claim of unauthorized electronic transfers ($4,500) without supporting evidence and did not provide the documents relied on.

elements.condition: Financial institution holding the consumer's account
Consumer gave notice of an error (unauthorized EFT)
Institution determined that no error occurred
Consumer requested the documents relied on
Institution provided a written explanation and copies of documents

evidence_quote: The institution's report of the results of its investigation shall include a written explanation of the institution's findings and shall note the consumer's right to request the documents that the institution relied on in making its determination. Upon request, the institution shall promptly provide copies of the documents.
rationale: The consumer challenges the bank's no-error determination and its refusal to share the evidence, which is the procedure in 1005.11(d)(1). Liability limits for unauthorized transfers (1005.6) are the runner-up, because the requested remedy is reversing the denial.

main_grievance: Debt buyer (LVNV, serviced by Resurgent) keeps reporting wrong balances and re-aged dates on three collection accounts that are being settled, and verified them after dispute; consumer wants them deleted.

elements.condition: Respondent is a debt collector (collects debts owed to another / purchased debts)
Communicates credit information to any person (reporting to CRAs)
Information is false (balances, dates) and collector knows or should know

evidence_quote: Communicate or threaten to communicate to any person credit information that the debt collector knows or should know is false, including the failure to communicate that a disputed debt is disputed.
rationale: The core complaint is a debt collector furnishing allegedly false balances and dates after being shown settlement proof, matching 1006.18(c)(2). The runner-up is 1006.18(b)(2)(i), falsely representing the amount of a debt.

main_grievance: Consumer lost money in a job/crypto scam after sending funds themselves through Cash App and other platforms; wants the platforms to recover the losses.

elements.condition: 1005.2(m): transfer initiated by a person other than the consumer without actual authority
elements.status: not met (consumer initiated the transfers, induced by fraud)

governing_law_if_none: No specific in-scope rule; authorized-push-payment fraud is outside Reg E error resolution (possibly UDAAP / state law)
rationale: Reg E error resolution and liability limits cover unauthorized transfers. 1005.2(m) excludes transfers the consumer initiated, even when tricked by a scammer. No in-scope section imposes a duty to reverse them.

main_grievance: Mortgage servicer mishandled the escrow account (did not adjust for an insurance increase), creating a large shortage, and has not provided the promised escrow analysis or explanation.

elements.condition: Escrow accounting/analysis duties are in Reg Z
elements.status: not met (they are in RESPA / Reg X 1024.17)

governing_law_if_none: RESPA / Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.17 (escrow accounts) and 1024.35-.36 (error notices, information requests); not in corpus
rationale: Escrow analyses, shortages, and servicer responses to error notices are governed by RESPA/Reg X, which is outside our four parts. Reg Z periodic statement rules (1026.41) do not address escrow analysis.

main_grievance: Consumer paid off a vehicle loan but never received the car title.

elements.condition: Title release after payoff is addressed by an in-scope section

governing_law_if_none: State motor vehicle title / lien release law
rationale: Lien and title release after payoff is governed by state law. None of Reg E, Z, V, or F imposes a title-release duty.

main_grievance: Federal student loan servicer has not executed an approved Borrower Defense discharge.

elements.condition: Federal student loan discharge processing is covered by Reg E/Z/V/F

governing_law_if_none: Higher Education Act; Department of Education regulations (34 CFR Part 685, borrower defense)
rationale: Borrower Defense discharges of federal Direct Loans are governed by Department of Education rules, outside the four CFPB regulations in our corpus.

main_grievance: $20,000 was deposited into and withdrawn from a Wells Fargo account the consumer says they never knew about (apparent identity theft); wants further action.

elements.condition: Transfers from an account established by the consumer (Reg E)
elements.status: unknown (consumer says they did not know of the account)

elements.condition: Consumer suffered a loss from their own account

governing_law_if_none: Bank fraud / account opened through identity theft at the bank; state law. Facts too sparse
rationale: The narrative is two lines and describes an account the consumer did not open, so it is not clearly the consumer's account under Reg E. Best guess NONE (identity theft); low confidence.

main_grievance: Unauthorized charges on a government benefit prepaid card after the wallet was stolen; the dispute was denied, and the consumer wants reimbursement.

elements.condition: Card used to access a consumer account for EFTs (government benefit / prepaid account)
Transfers initiated by a thief without authority (unauthorized EFT)
Consumer gave timely notice of the error
Institution investigated and determined no error

evidence_quote: A financial institution shall investigate promptly and, except as otherwise provided in this paragraph (c), shall determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving a notice of error.
rationale: Unauthorized card transactions reported promptly and denied fall under Reg E error resolution. Following the convention for denied unauthorized-transfer claims, the label is 1005.11, with liability limits 1005.6 also relevant. 1005.15 and 1005.18 modify these rules for government benefit and prepaid accounts.

main_grievance: Template dispute asking Equifax to investigate and remove inaccurate or unverifiable items and inquiries.

elements.condition: Respondent is a consumer reporting agency
Consumer disputed the completeness or accuracy of an item in their file
Agency failed to reasonably reinvestigate or correct

evidence_quote: if the completeness or accuracy of any item of information contained in a consumer's file at a consumer reporting agency is disputed by the consumer and the consumer notifies the agency directly, or indirectly through a reseller, of such dispute, the agency shall, free of charge, conduct a reasonable reinvestigation to determine whether the disputed information is inaccurate
rationale: Template dispute to a CRA asking it to investigate and remove unverifiable items: CRA reinvestigation, 1681i(a)(1).

main_grievance: Estate administrator says the bank wrongly released a deceased customer's funds under a small-estate affidavit and is withholding account records.

elements.condition: Consumer's EFT error or credit issue under Reg E/Z

governing_law_if_none: State probate / small estate law; deposit account agreement
rationale: Disbursement of a decedent's funds and records for an estate administrator are governed by state probate law, not by the CFPB regulations in the corpus.

main_grievance: Account takeover: someone changed the consumer's Chime login and sent all funds ($930) to a stranger; Chime denied the fraud dispute within hours.

elements.condition: EFT from a consumer asset account
Initiated by another person without authority (unauthorized EFT)
Consumer gave notice of the error
Institution investigated reasonably before determining no error

evidence_quote: A financial institution shall investigate promptly and, except as otherwise provided in this paragraph (c), shall determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving a notice of error.
rationale: An unauthorized transfer after account takeover is a Reg E error, and the consumer disputes a hasty denial, so error resolution 1005.11 governs. Consumer liability limits (1005.6) are the runner-up.

main_grievance: Store card issuer paid 5% instead of the advertised 10% promotional rewards on a qualifying purchase and refuses to correct it.

elements.condition: Reward promotion terms are a Reg Z disclosure or billing-error matter

governing_law_if_none: Card agreement / promotion terms; UDAAP (12 U.S.C. 5531) and state consumer protection law
rationale: The dispute concerns rewards earned under a promotion, not an extension of credit shown on a statement. No Reg Z section governs reward fulfilment.

main_grievance: A medical debt was paid in full to the debt buyer, but the original creditor that sold it still reports a $6,000 balance; consumer wants it updated to $0.

elements.condition: Original creditor regularly furnishes information to CRAs
Furnisher knows its reported balance is not accurate (account sold and paid)

evidence_quote: shall promptly notify the consumer reporting agency of that determination and provide to the agency any corrections to that information
rationale: The inaccurate $6,000 balance comes from the original creditor as furnisher; its duty to correct and update is 1681s-2(a)(2). The respondent is the debt buyer, so confidence is low.

main_grievance: HELOC servicer did not credit a $2,200 payment that cleared; the consumer sent a written dispute and wants the payment applied plus interest refunded.

elements.condition: Open-end credit plan (HELOC)
Statement reflects creditor's failure to credit a payment
Written billing error notice received within 60 days of the statement
elements.status: unknown (written dispute sent; timing not stated)

evidence_quote: A reflection on a periodic statement of the creditor's failure to credit properly a payment or other credit issued to the consumer's account.
rationale: A HELOC is open-end credit, a missed payment credit is a billing error under 1026.13(a)(4), and the consumer sent a written dispute. 1026.10(a) (credit payments on receipt) is the runner-up.

main_grievance: Auto finance company holds a contract tainted by dealer fraud (warranty premium withheld) and its repossession agent damaged the vehicle; consumer demands rescission and refund.

elements.condition: Dealer fraud, warranty, or repossession damage governed by Reg E/Z/V/F

governing_law_if_none: FTC Holder Rule (16 CFR 433.2), state UCC repossession and consumer protection law
rationale: The claims (dealer misrepresentation, holder liability, repossession damage) arise under the FTC Holder Rule and state law. No Reg Z disclosure issue is raised.

main_grievance: Payday loan borrower did not know the very high interest rate (payments barely reduce principal); lender allegedly unlicensed in Washington.

elements.condition: Closed-end consumer credit from a creditor
APR disclosed using that term before consummation
elements.status: unknown (consumer says they did not know the rate)

evidence_quote: The annual percentage rate, using that term, and a brief description such as
rationale: The in-scope grievance is not knowing the cost of credit, and Reg Z requires disclosing the APR for closed-end loans (1026.18(e)). Licensing and usury are state law. Whether the disclosure was actually missing is unknown.

main_grievance: Private student loan lender demands payments despite approved in-school deferment and debited about $300 from the consumer's bank account without authorization.

elements.condition: Deferment entitlement governed by an in-scope section
Unauthorized preauthorized debit (1005.10(b)) as the main grievance

governing_law_if_none: Private student loan contract (deferment terms); state law
rationale: The main grievance is the lender ignoring a contractual in-school deferment, which no in-scope section governs. The unauthorized debit would implicate Reg E 1005.10(b) (written authorization for preauthorized transfers), so it is the runner-up.

main_grievance: Government benefit prepaid card dispute over funds moved by a companion cardholder is unresolved past 45 days, with provisional credit promised and then reversed.

elements.condition: Consumer asserted an error on an account accessed by card
Institution took more than 10 business days and handled provisional credit
Investigation completed within 45 days

evidence_quote: If the financial institution is unable to complete its investigation within 10 business days, the institution may take up to 45 days from receipt of a notice of error to investigate and determine whether an error occurred, provided the institution does the following:
rationale: The complaint is about the error-resolution timeline and provisional credit, governed by 1005.11(c)(2), as modified for government benefit accounts by 1005.15. Whether the companion transfer was unauthorized is doubtful, since the consumer furnished the card (1005.2(m)(1)), but the procedural duty still applies.

main_grievance: Equifax did not block fraudulent accounts and inquiries after the consumer submitted an identity theft report.

elements.condition: Respondent is a consumer reporting agency
Consumer identified information as resulting from identity theft
Consumer supplied proof of identity and an identity theft report

evidence_quote: a consumer reporting agency shall block the reporting of any information in the file of a consumer that the consumer identifies as information that resulted from an alleged identity theft
rationale: Equifax did not block accounts after receiving a police report and dispute about identity theft: the block duty in 1681c-2(a).

main_grievance: Money was stolen from the consumer's debit card, which they attribute to eavesdropping software.

elements.condition: EFT from consumer account via debit card
Initiated without the consumer's authority
Consumer notified the institution

evidence_quote: A consumer may be held liable, within the limitations described in paragraph (b) of this section, for an unauthorized electronic fund transfer involving the consumer's account only if the financial institution has provided the disclosures required by
rationale: The narrative alleges unauthorized debit card transfers but describes no dispute handling, so consumer liability for unauthorized transfers (1005.6) is the closest duty. The very sparse facts mean low confidence.

main_grievance: A $4,000 collection for a credit card the consumer never had appeared after an identity theft attempt; the named collection agency seems not to exist.

elements.condition: Respondent furnishes information to CRAs
Information alleged to result from identity theft
Consumer or CRA notified the furnisher of the identity theft

evidence_quote: A person that furnishes information to any consumer reporting agency shall have in place reasonable procedures to respond to any notification that it receives from a consumer reporting agency
rationale: A creditor reporting a collection on an identity-theft account implicates furnisher identity-theft duties in 1681s-2(a)(6); sparse facts mean low confidence.

main_grievance: Victim of a fake e-commerce investment platform sent money from Capital One via Bitcoin; the bank denied the dispute because the consumer authorized the transfers.

elements.condition: 1005.2(m): transfer initiated by someone other than the consumer without authority
elements.status: not met (consumer initiated the transfers under fraud)

governing_law_if_none: No in-scope rule for consumer-authorized scam payments (possibly UDAAP / state law)
rationale: As with item 18390509, transfers the consumer made themselves under a scammer's inducement are excluded from Reg E's unauthorized-transfer protections, so no in-scope section requires reversal.

main_grievance: Consumer asks Chase to remove an admittedly accurate 30-day late payment as a goodwill adjustment.

elements.condition: Reported information is inaccurate
elements.status: not met (consumer concedes the payment was late)

governing_law_if_none: None: no legal duty to remove accurate information (FCRA permits accurate reporting)
rationale: The consumer concedes the late payment. Goodwill removal is discretionary, and no in-scope section requires a furnisher to delete accurate data.

main_grievance: Mortgage servicer mishandled a complete loss mitigation application, with shifting document demands, no continuity of contact, and foreclosure risk.

elements.condition: Loss mitigation and continuity-of-contact duties in Reg Z

governing_law_if_none: RESPA / Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.41 (loss mitigation), 1024.40 (continuity of contact), 1024.35-.36; not in corpus
rationale: Loss mitigation evaluation and continuity of contact are Reg X servicing rules. The consumer's cite of 1026.40 for continuity of contact is mistaken (1026.40 covers HELOC disclosures).

main_grievance: Lessor has not delivered the title for a lease vehicle paid off more than three years ago.

elements.condition: Title release governed by an in-scope section

governing_law_if_none: State motor vehicle title law; lease contract
rationale: Title delivery after payoff is a state-law and contract matter; no in-scope regulation applies.

main_grievance: Personal loan lender keeps reporting the account as past due after its duplicate retry debit was reversed by the consumer's bank; consumer told the lender directly and wants the account shown current.

elements.condition: Dispute made directly to the furnisher
elements.status: met (consumer communicated the dispute to the lender)

elements.condition: Dispute relates to payment status on an account with the furnisher
Dispute sent to a proper address with sufficient information (1022.43(d))

evidence_quote: The consumer's performance or other conduct concerning an account or other relationship with the furnisher, such as direct disputes relating to the current payment status, high balance, date a payment was made, the amount of a payment made, or the date an account was opened or closed; or
rationale: The consumer disputes the past-due status directly with the lender that furnishes it, which is the direct-dispute duty in 1022.43(a)(3). The duplicate debit itself was resolved by the consumer's bank.

main_grievance: Federal student loan servicer has not posted about $1,900-$2,000 in payments despite nearly a year of escalations.

elements.condition: Federal student loan servicing covered by Reg Z/E/V/F

governing_law_if_none: Higher Education Act; Department of Education servicing contract and 34 CFR Part 685
rationale: Posting payments to federal Direct Loans is governed by Department of Education rules and servicing contracts, outside the four CFPB regulations.

main_grievance: A Vanilla Visa gift card bought with cash was rejected by online merchants, and the refund would take weeks.

elements.condition: 1005.20 gift card rule addresses merchant acceptance or refund timing
elements.status: not met (1005.20 covers fees, expiration, disclosures)

governing_law_if_none: Card terms; state consumer protection law
rationale: Gift cards fall under Reg E only through 1005.20's limits on fees and expiration. Merchant acceptance and refund timing are not addressed by any in-scope section.

main_grievance: Consumer demands that Experian remove negative items they do not recognize.

elements.condition: Respondent is a consumer reporting agency
Consumer disputed the completeness or accuracy of an item in their file
Agency failed to reasonably reinvestigate or correct

evidence_quote: if the completeness or accuracy of any item of information contained in a consumer's file at a consumer reporting agency is disputed by the consumer and the consumer notifies the agency directly, or indirectly through a reseller, of such dispute, the agency shall, free of charge, conduct a reasonable reinvestigation to determine whether the disputed information is inaccurate
rationale: Dispute of unrecognized negative items lodged with Experian: CRA reinvestigation duty.

main_grievance: Unauthorized debit card purchases ($10,000) on a Wells Fargo account; the bank closed the dispute and refuses to reopen it.

elements.condition: Debit card EFTs from a consumer account
Initiated without the consumer's authority
Consumer gave notice of error
Institution reasonably investigated before closing

evidence_quote: A financial institution shall investigate promptly and, except as otherwise provided in this paragraph (c), shall determine whether an error occurred within 10 business days of receiving a notice of error.
rationale: Following the convention for denied or closed unauthorized-transfer disputes, Reg E error resolution 1005.11 governs. The narrative's mention of returned merchandise muddies whether the transfers were truly unauthorized.

main_grievance: Consumer disputes a collection account as not theirs and requests full validation/verification from the debt collector, and contact in writing only.

elements.condition: Respondent is a debt collector
Consumer disputed the debt in writing
Dispute submitted within the validation period

evidence_quote: Upon receipt of a dispute submitted by the consumer in writing within the validation period, a debt collector must cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion of the debt, until the debt collector:
rationale: The template letter is a written dispute demanding verification, matching the collector's duty in 1006.38(d)(2) to stop collecting until it sends verification. 1006.34 (the validation notice) is the runner-up.

main_grievance: Receiving institution returned the consumer's misdirected domestic wires and charged $50 per wire without permission.

elements.condition: Transfer is an electronic fund transfer under Reg E
elements.status: not met (wire transfers via Fedwire are excluded from Reg E's EFT definition)

governing_law_if_none: UCC Article 4A / Fedwire rules; account agreement fee terms
rationale: Domestic wire transfers are outside Reg E. The return-wire fee is a matter of fee terms and funds-transfer law, not an in-scope regulation.

main_grievance: PayPal Credit applied the consumer's payments to longer 24-month promotional balances instead of the 12-month promotion that is ending, leaving it unpaid.

elements.condition: Credit card account under an open-end (not home-secured) plan
Payments exceed the required minimum payment
Issuer allocated the excess contrary to the APR or deferred-interest rules

evidence_quote: when a consumer makes a payment in excess of the required minimum periodic payment for a credit card account under an open-end (not home-secured) consumer credit plan, the card issuer must allocate the excess amount first to the balance with the highest annual percentage rate
rationale: The dispute is how payments are allocated among promotional balances, the subject of 1026.53. Whether the promotions are deferred-interest, which would trigger 1026.53(b), is not stated.

main_grievance: Lender added a high origination fee (discount points to buy down the rate) at closing that the consumer did not request or know about.

elements.condition: Closed-end mortgage subject to Loan Estimate/Closing Disclosure rules
Charge on the Closing Disclosure exceeds the amount on the Loan Estimate
No valid changed circumstance or consumer-requested change
elements.status: unknown (consumer says they did not request a buydown)

evidence_quote: An estimated closing cost disclosed pursuant to paragraph (e) of this section is in good faith if the charge paid by or imposed on the consumer does not exceed the amount originally disclosed under paragraph (e)(1)(i) of this section
rationale: An unrequested increase in origination charges at closing is tested against the Loan Estimate's good-faith tolerance in 1026.19(e)(3). Without the Loan Estimate figures, confidence is low; the Closing Disclosure content rule (1026.38) is the runner-up.

main_grievance: Repossession agent for the auto lender trespassed into a gated area, damaged property, and injured a person (breach of the peace).

elements.condition: Repossession conduct governed by an in-scope section

governing_law_if_none: State UCC 9-609 (breach of the peace), state tort and consumer fraud law
rationale: Self-help repossession limits are state law. Reg F does not apply to the creditor's own enforcement of security interests except for 1006.22(e), which needs a debt collector.

main_grievance: Bank charged a higher interest margin than the business line of credit agreement specifies.

elements.condition: Consumer credit (personal, family, household purpose)

governing_law_if_none: Loan contract / state law (business-purpose credit is exempt from Regulation Z)
rationale: The account is a business line of credit, and Reg Z covers consumer credit only, so no in-scope section governs the rate dispute.

main_grievance: A collection agency is collecting and reporting a private student loan the consumer never applied for (apparent identity theft), damaging their credit.

elements.condition: Respondent is a debt collector
Communicates credit information to CRAs
Collector knows or should know the information is false, or fails to report it as disputed

evidence_quote: Communicate or threaten to communicate to any person credit information that the debt collector knows or should know is false, including the failure to communicate that a disputed debt is disputed.
rationale: The grievance is a collector reporting a disputed, allegedly fraudulent debt, which matches 1006.18(c)(2) as in item 20536937. The duty to verify disputed debts (1006.38) is the runner-up.

main_grievance: Unemployment benefit prepaid card charged ATM withdrawal fees the consumer was told would be free, and some withdrawn amounts appear to be missing; only a partial refund was given.

elements.condition: Government benefit / prepaid account accessed by card
Consumer asserts incorrect transfers or amounts
Consumer notified the institution

evidence_quote: An incorrect electronic fund transfer to or from the consumer's account;
rationale: The consumer disputes fees and amounts withdrawn and contacted the issuer, which is closest to a Reg E error. If the grievance is that fees contradicted the fee disclosures, 1005.15 (government benefit account disclosures) applies instead. The garbled facts mean low confidence.

main_grievance: Brokerage-affiliated bank froze the consumer's account and funds after an incoming ACH transfer and keeps losing the verification documents.

elements.condition: Account restriction or funds availability governed by Reg E/Z/V/F

governing_law_if_none: Regulation CC (12 CFR 229) funds availability; deposit account agreement; BSA/KYC verification
rationale: Freezing an account pending verification is not an EFT error and is governed by funds-availability rules and the account agreement, outside our corpus.

main_grievance: Consumer asks TransUnion to block and delete unauthorized accounts from identity theft.

elements.condition: Respondent is a consumer reporting agency
Consumer identified information as resulting from identity theft
Consumer supplied proof of identity and an identity theft report

evidence_quote: a consumer reporting agency shall block the reporting of any information in the file of a consumer that the consumer identifies as information that resulted from an alleged identity theft
rationale: Explicit request to TransUnion to block and delete identity-theft accounts with a report: 1681c-2(a).

main_grievance: Consumer was charged for a Kikoff annual subscription they did not knowingly sign up for, and it now shows as a collection.

elements.condition: Respondent is a third-party debt collector (Reg F)
Unrequested credit account governed by an in-scope section

governing_law_if_none: Subscription / negative-option and state consumer protection law
rationale: Kikoff is collecting its own subscription charge, so Reg F's validation notice duty (the CFPB issue category) does not apply. The sparse facts give no clear in-scope duty.

main_grievance: A phone scammer posing as the card issuer led to a fictitious $2,900 charge on the consumer's Barclays credit card; the consumer reported it and the issuer is sending dispute documents.

elements.condition: Use of a credit card by someone other than the cardholder without authority
elements.status: unknown (scammer controlled the consumer's phone; may involve consumer participation)

elements.condition: Cardholder notified the issuer

evidence_quote: The liability of a cardholder for unauthorized use of a credit card shall not exceed the lesser of $50 or the amount of money, property, labor, or services obtained by the unauthorized use before notification to the card issuer
rationale: A fraudulent credit card charge reported to the issuer is governed by the unauthorized-use liability limit in 1026.12(b). The narrative is cut off and the dispute is still pending, so billing-error resolution (1026.13) is the runner-up.

main_grievance: Person who opened a PayPal account abroad using an SSN found online cannot pass phone verification and wants the limited account restored.

elements.condition: Consumer right under an in-scope section to regain account access

governing_law_if_none: Platform terms of service / identity verification (KYC); no in-scope duty
rationale: Account access and identity verification for a PayPal account are not governed by any in-scope regulation, and the narrative admits using another person's SSN.

main_grievance: New mortgage servicer has not handled the consumer's request to impound (escrow) property taxes and is seen as untrustworthy.

elements.condition: Escrow establishment/servicing duties in Reg Z
elements.status: not met (RESPA / Reg X escrow rules)

governing_law_if_none: RESPA / Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.17 (escrow accounts); servicing transfer rules 1024.33; not in corpus
rationale: Escrow requests to a mortgage servicer fall under Reg X, which is outside our corpus. Reg Z's mortgage transfer disclosure (1026.39) is only tangential.

main_grievance: PayPal advertised a 'Pay in 4' promotion, then denied the consumer's application without a real reason, citing suspicious activity.

elements.condition: Credit denial reasons governed by Reg Z
elements.status: not met (adverse action notices are Reg B)

elements.condition: Pay-in-4 is credit subject to a finance charge
elements.status: not met (typically no finance charge, four or fewer installments)

governing_law_if_none: ECOA / Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9 (adverse action notice); not in corpus
rationale: The grievance is a credit denial without stated reasons, which is an ECOA/Reg B matter. The advertising angle would point to Reg Z 1026.16, but Pay-in-4 plans generally fall outside Reg Z.

main_grievance: Auto lender ignored written disputes over payment application and total-loss calculations, then reported the loan past due, kept calling, and took a $250 offset from checking.

elements.condition: Direct dispute to the furnisher
Dispute relates to terms or balance of the debt with the furnisher
Furnisher failed to investigate before reporting

evidence_quote: The terms of a credit account or other debt with the furnisher, such as direct disputes relating to the type of account, principal balance, scheduled payment amount on an account, or the amount of the credit limit on an open-end account;
rationale: The in-scope element is the creditor reporting a delinquency while the consumer's direct dispute about the balance was pending (1022.43). The offset and collection calls by the creditor itself fall outside Reg F, and Reg Z's offset rule covers credit cards only. Mixed grievances mean low confidence.

main_grievance: Federal student loan servicer won't say whether it notified the borrower that interest would resume during SAVE-related forbearance.

elements.condition: Federal student loan servicing covered by an in-scope section

governing_law_if_none: Higher Education Act; Department of Education rules and servicing contract
rationale: Federal Direct Loan forbearance and interest notices are governed by Department of Education rules, outside the corpus.

main_grievance: A settlement payout prepaid card cannot be used for purchases, and the provider does not answer calls or emails.

elements.condition: Card usability / customer service governed by Reg E prepaid rules
elements.status: not met (1005.18 covers disclosures, error resolution, liability)

governing_law_if_none: Card program terms; state law (possibly unclaimed property / settlement administration)
rationale: The problem is that the card is not accepted and support is unresponsive, which no in-scope section requires. If an error (incorrect transfer) were alleged, 1005.18 with 1005.11 would apply.

main_grievance: Consumer's disputes to CRAs, validation letters to collectors, and goodwill requests to Capital One (about late payments) went unanswered; wants items deleted.

elements.condition: Capital One furnished the disputed late-payment data
Capital One received notice of the dispute from a CRA
Capital One failed to investigate

evidence_quote: conduct an investigation with respect to the disputed information;
rationale: Against Capital One, the in-scope claim is the disputed 90-day late passed through TransUnion, triggering the furnisher investigation duty in 1681s-2(b). The goodwill requests themselves create no duty.

main_grievance: Debt buyer never answered the consumer's written verification requests about a debt the consumer does not recognize, then sued them.

elements.condition: Respondent is a debt collector
Consumer disputed in writing
Dispute within the validation period
elements.status: unknown (consumer says no validation notice was received)

elements.condition: Collector continued collection without sending verification

evidence_quote: Upon receipt of a dispute submitted by the consumer in writing within the validation period, a debt collector must cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion of the debt, until the debt collector:
rationale: Written verification requests ignored before a lawsuit match the dispute-response duty in 1006.38(d)(2). The claim that no validation notice was ever sent makes 1006.34 the runner-up.

main_grievance: A spa opened a Synchrony credit account in the consumer's name without consent, and the consumer is billed for services never received.

elements.condition: Credit card issued
